name: holed stones

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Holed stones are symbolic objects. People used large rocks with natural holes to seal marriage vows across the Celtic lands. Loving couples clasped hands through the holes while pledging their troth. In some regions a church wedding was not valid unless the couple also spoke their vows at a holed stone. In Britain people call these formations Dobie stones. The name links them to the fairies of that name. The stones also served healing uses.
objective: Document holed stones as symbolic objects used in marriage vows.
